purpose: A bounded method for running the life of a home service contract after it is sold: keeping an accurate in-force book, guiding the client through a claim process the obligor controls without ever promising an outcome, decoding and responding proportionately to denials, testing honestly whether each account should renew, downgrade, move obligor or lapse, holding renewal, rate-change and cancellation conversations that disclose the bad parts, protecting vulnerable clients from silent renewals, and managing the reputation and referral consequences of a product class where partial and denied claims are structural.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the agent sells home service contracts as an appointed representative of an obligor and never decides, funds or adjudicates a claim

contract terms, renewal and auto-renew mechanics, cancellation and refund rights, and compensation schedules differ by obligor, product and jurisdiction and are read from the current documents per account rather than remembered
every quantity here (commission, renewal price, trade service fee, cap, persistency) is treated as a mechanism with named drivers and a per-account verification path, never as a stated figure
the agent has, or can build, one maintained record of the accounts they placed; nothing in this knowledge base is runnable from memory across a book of any size
the content is educational and operational for the seller, not personalized legal, insurance, tax or financial advice to any homeowner
exclusions: how service-contract products are structured as instruments (obligor and administrator roles, term, caps and service-fee design as mechanisms), obligor diligence, and the choice, economics and per-channel compliance class of distribution channels - that is the products-and-distribution knowledge base this one receives in-force accounts from

line-by-line reading of covered systems, exclusions, caps, waiting periods and pre-existing-condition clauses, the disclosure-first pre-sale conversation, matching a plan tier to a home at first sale, and the sale documentation packet - that is the coverage-terms and honest-disclosure knowledge base
adjudicating, litigating or predicting the outcome of any individual claim; the obligor decides claims under the contract and this knowledge base never asserts what will or will not be paid

asserting the registration, licensing, cancellation, refund, auto-renew, contact-consent or complaint-handling rules of any named jurisdiction; every such obligation appears as a class to verify with the applicable regulator, the obligor compliance function and counsel

quoting specific commission rates, renewal percentages, contract prices, trade service fees, cap amounts, persistency percentages or book multiples as facts; each appears only as a mechanism with its drivers and its verification path
personalized legal, insurance, tax or financial advice to a homeowner, landlord, property manager or referral partner
performing repairs, dispatching or managing contractors, and operating the obligor claim, billing or underwriting systems
fear-based selling, manufactured urgency, incentivised or fabricated reviews, and any retention practice that obstructs, delays or conditions a stated cancellation request

competency_questions.question: Once the contract is in force, what exactly is the agent to the client during a claim, and what may the agent never say?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POST_SALE_ROLE_CHARTER states the guide-not-adjudicator role, the response commitment and the never-say list, and CLAIM_ADVOCACY_LIMITS draws the line between legitimate advocacy and misrepresentation

competency_questions.question: What must the in-force book record per contract so that no renewal, lapse or claim is discovered late?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IN_FORCE_BOOK_LEDGER lists the per-contract fields, the reconciliation cadence against the obligor in-force report, and the consent status that governs contact

competency_questions.question: How does what the client was told at sale get carried into the claim and renewal conversations, and what happens when it does not match the contract?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXPECTATION_BASELINE_CARRY defines the dated expectation record, when it is read, and the plain-admission-and-repair rule when a gap is found

competency_questions.question: How does renewal-side compensation actually come to exist on this book, and what reduces, reverses or removes it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_COMPENSATION_MECHANICS names the mechanism components (renewal-side schedule, agent-of-record and orphaning, chargeback window, direct-bill crediting, tier-change base) with the per-obligor verification path and no invented figures

competency_questions.question: What happens between a system failing and a claim resolving, where does it stall, and how is the client kept informed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLAIM_LIFECYCLE_MAP gives the per-obligor stages, stall points and escalation contact classes, and CLAIM_STATUS_COMMUNICATION sets the cadence and written-summary practice

competency_questions.question: What does the agent do, in order, on the first call from a client whose system just failed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIRST_CALL_TRIAGE gives the fixed sequence from safety check through in-force and waiting-period verification to intake instructions, service-fee statement and the who-decides sentence

competency_questions.question: A claim was denied - how is the reason decoded, which denials are worth contesting, and what is the sequence for responding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DENIAL_DECODING classifies the clause class and the dispute type including the correct-and-final class, and DENIAL_RESPONSE_PLAYBOOK gives the evidence, single-submission, escalation and honest-acceptance sequence

competency_questions.question: How does the agent help a client evaluate a cash-in-lieu offer, a cap-limited authorization or a repair where the client wanted replacement?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PARTIAL_OUTCOME_EVALUATION lays out what the offer covers, the non-covered adjacent costs, what acceptance forecloses, and the boundary against appraising or advising what to accept

competency_questions.question: How is it decided, honestly and per account, whether this client should renew, change tier, change obligor or drop the plan - and how is the do-not-renew message delivered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_VALUE_TEST assembles remaining covered risk, account history, changed price and the client position into a four-way recommendation with a recorded reason, and NON_RENEWAL_ADVICE gives the recurring cases and the delivery and recording practice

competency_questions.question: When is the renewal conversation scheduled, and how is a changed price, service fee, cap or tier presented without hiding the delta?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_CYCLE_CALENDAR derives the touch schedule from each contract's own dates, notice windows and consent status, and RATE_CHANGE_CONVERSATION requires a change-by-change comparison to the prior term paired with the value-test recommendation

competency_questions.question: Which retention moves are legitimate, and how must a client who says they want to cancel be handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETENTION_LEVER_MAP separates fit-and-clarity levers from fear-and-friction practices, and CANCELLATION_AND_SAVE_ETHICS states the cancellation mechanics per product and the process-it-do-not-gate-it rule

competency_questions.question: What extra care applies when the client is elderly, bereaved, cognitively impaired or in financial distress at renewal or during a claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VULNERABLE_CLIENT_POST_SALE_CARE requires comprehension confirmation in the client's own words, restraint on auto-renew reliance, consented trusted-contact practice, a no-upgrade-during-crisis rule and escalation of suspected exploitation as a class

competency_questions.question: Where does reputation damage in this product class actually come from, and how are public complaints and referral partners handled without breaching client privacy or arguing a claim in public?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPUTATION_RISK_MODEL separates product, obligor-service and agent-conduct complaint streams with leading indicators, PUBLIC_COMPLAINT_RESPONSE gives the no-detail public reply and offline continuation pattern, and REFERRAL_REPUTATION_LOOP covers partner briefing and the consented feedback loop

competency_questions.question: How does the agent use their own book evidence to decide whether to keep selling an obligor, and what does a periodic book review measure and act on?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OBLIGOR_PERFORMANCE_REVIEW assembles per-obligor claim evidence into a dated keep, restrict, pause or stop decision, and BOOK_HEALTH_REVIEW turns cohort metrics into interventions with owners and dates

glossary.definition: The share of in-force contracts that survive their renewal date rather than lapsing or cancelling, measured by cohort (origin channel, obligor, tier, year written); the health measure of a service-contract book, and misleading on its own because it rises when clients are renewed who should have been advised to lapse.

The party the obligor has recorded as owning the client relationship on a contract, which is what routes renewal-side compensation and service correspondence; it can move by client request, on transfer of the home, on appointment termination, or under house-account rules, and each obligor defines that movement differently.

The period after a contract is written or renewed during which a cancellation, refund or non-payment reverses compensation already paid to the agent; its length, its pro-rata or full-reversal basis and its interaction with claims already paid are read from the current compensation schedule per obligor.

A renewal that continues automatically on the stored payment instrument unless the client acts, usually with an obligor notice obligation before a rate or term change takes effect; efficient for the book and the main mechanism by which a client can end up paying for a plan they no longer understand or want.

The obligor or administrator statement naming which contract clause a claim was declined under; obtaining it in writing is the precondition for classifying the denial, for any escalation, and for telling the client honestly whether the answer can change.

An offer to pay the client an amount instead of performing the covered repair or replacement, valued on the basis the contract describes; it settles the obligor obligation and leaves the client to arrange the work, which is where non-covered adjacent costs surface.

The state in which a per-system, per-term or aggregate limit has been consumed by prior authorizations, so a later failure in the same term is limited or unpayable even though the system is nominally covered; a leading cause of the second-claim disappointment that drives renewal loss.

An in-force contract whose writing agent is no longer appointed, no longer recorded, or no longer servicing it, leaving the client with no named person to call and the renewal to the obligor direct-bill process; the state most books drift toward without deliberate maintenance.

The dated summary carried forward from the sale of what the client was actually walked through - which exclusions, caps, waiting periods and fees were named, which tier was recommended and why, and which of the home's risks were called out as uncovered; the reference point for every later claim and renewal conversation.

A named step in the obligor or administrator process above routine claim handling (supervisor review, claims escalation desk, formal complaint intake), each with its own contact route and expected response; escalation credibility is finite, so the stage is chosen to match the dispute class rather than the client's volume.

nodes.definition: Fix, in writing and in the words the client actually hears, what the agent is and is not once the contract is in force. The agent is the client's guide through a process the obligor controls: explaining what the contract says, telling the client exactly how and where to open a claim, chasing status, insisting on a written reason for any decline, and translating that reason back into plain language. The agent is not the adjudicator and is not the obligor's shield: no coverage outcome is promised, no decline is defended reflexively, and no claim result is announced to a client before the obligor has made it. The charter names the sentences the agent will say at first contact after a failure, the sentences the agent will never say (that will definitely be covered, they always deny that, leave it with me and I will get it approved), the response time the client can expect from the agent, and the point at which the agent points the client to the obligor's own complaint stage or to the external complaint route that supervises service contracts where the client lives - named as a class, with verify current rules in your jurisdiction attached. Every other unit of work in this knowledge base is an application of this charter.

included: the client-facing statement of who decides claims and what the agent will do
the never-say list and the agent response-time commitment
the handoff points to obligor complaint stages and external complaint routes as classes
excluded: adjudicating or funding any claim
the pre-sale disclosure conversation, which belongs to the coverage-terms knowledge base
asserting the specific complaint or regulator rules of any named jurisdiction

pros.claim: A stated promise boundary makes the first decline a survivable conversation instead of a betrayal
pros.example: a client who was told at sale that the agent cannot decide claims hears a decline as the contract working rather than as the agent having lied

cons.claim: The charter withholds exactly the reassurance a client wants mid-failure, and some buyers read an honest boundary as weak commitment
cons.example: a homeowner standing in a cold house asks for a yes, hears a description of the process, and takes their next purchase to an agent who promises

failure_modes: improvising a coverage opinion on the phone that the obligor later contradicts
sliding into the obligor's defence counsel role and losing the client the moment a decline lands
writing the charter and never saying it aloud at sale or at first claim
acceptance_tests: the charter states in client-facing language who decides claims, what the agent will do within a stated response time, and the never-say list
every in-force account file shows the charter language was delivered to the client at or before the first claim contact
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes its claim intake or complaint channel
a client complaint alleges the agent promised a coverage outcome
the external complaint or regulator route class for service contracts in a served jurisdiction changes

base.update_signal: a client dispute, obligor audit or complaint file shows the agent's stated role differed from what was actually said during a claim

nodes.definition: Maintain one authoritative record of every contract the agent placed and is still responsible for, because renewals and claims both fail first as data problems. Per contract the ledger carries the obligor and administrator, the plan tier, the effective and expiry dates, whether the term auto-renews and what notice window attaches, the payment instrument and its expiry, the trade service fee level, the property and whether the client still owns it, the origin channel and referring partner, the contact-consent status and preferred channel, the expectation record from the sale, and every claim the agent knows of with its date, system, stage and outcome. It is reconciled on a set cadence against the obligor's own in-force report, because the two disagree constantly: direct-billed renewals, obligor-side cancellations for failed payment, mid-term transfers on a home sale and agent-of-record changes all move accounts without telling the agent. The ledger is the object every later unit reads from; a renewal calendar, a claim history, an obligor performance review and a book review are all views of it, and none of them can be reconstructed from memory once a book is more than a few dozen accounts.

included: the per-contract field set including dates, renewal mechanism, payment and consent status
the reconciliation cadence against the obligor in-force report
the running claim log per account
excluded: the obligor claim system of record
commission accounting and rate mechanics, which sit in the compensation node
pre-sale lead and pipeline management, which belongs to the distribution knowledge base

pros.claim: Reconciliation finds accounts that lapsed without anyone telling the agent while the client still believes they are covered
pros.example: an obligor-side cancellation after a failed card surfaces at reconciliation rather than at the client's next failure

cons.claim: The ledger is unpaid upkeep on the day it is done, and a stale field is worse than a missing one because it is acted on
cons.example: a renewal call placed to a homeowner who sold the property six months earlier

failure_modes: treating the obligor portal as the only record and losing the entire book when an appointment ends
logging claims only when they go badly, which biases every later obligor comparison
holding contact data with no defensible consent basis and contacting on it
acceptance_tests: every in-force account carries obligor, dates, renewal mechanism, payment status, consent status and a claim log
the last reconciliation date against each obligor in-force report is within the stated cadence
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes the format or frequency of its in-force reporting
an appointment or agent-of-record status changes
contact-consent obligations change for a served jurisdiction

base.update_signal: a reconciliation run that finds a material share of accounts in a different state than the ledger recorded

nodes.definition: Carry the record of what the client was actually told at sale into the post-sale relationship and use it as the reference point for every claim and renewal conversation. The disclosure conversation itself belongs to the coverage-terms knowledge base; this unit owns what happens to its residue afterwards. The record is dated and specific: which exclusions, caps, waiting periods and fee terms were walked through, which tier was recommended and on what reasoning, what the client said about the age and history of their systems, and which of this home's realistic risks were named out loud as not covered. At first claim the agent reads it before speaking, because the gap between what the client believes and what the contract says is the best available predictor of whether a decline becomes a complaint. Where the record shows an expectation was never set - a system the client assumed was included, a cap they never registered - the agent says so plainly rather than defending a disclosure that did not happen, and repairs it at the renewal conversation. The same record protects the agent when a client misremembers, which is why it must be written to be honest rather than written to be defensible.

included: carrying the dated expectation summary into the ledger
reading it before every claim and renewal conversation
admitting and repairing a gap the record exposes
excluded: running the pre-sale disclosure conversation and building the sale documentation packet
interpreting clause text line by line
rewriting the record after a dispute has started

pros.claim: A mismatch found before the claim call converts an ambush into a prepared conversation
pros.example: the file shows the roof-leak exclusion was never discussed, so the agent leads with that admission instead of being cornered by it an hour later

cons.claim: An honest record can be evidence against the agent's own sale, which tempts thin self-serving summaries that help nobody
cons.example: a one-line note reading disclosures reviewed, which proves nothing at the moment a client says they were never told about the cap

failure_modes: no record at all, so the first decline becomes one person's word against another
treating the record as a legal shield rather than a service tool and never acting on what it reveals
finding a gap and letting it stand until the renewal is lost
acceptance_tests: each account carries a dated expectation summary naming the exclusions, caps, waiting periods and fees actually walked through and the tier reasoning
claim and renewal call logs show the record was read before the conversation, and any gap found is recorded with the repair action
revisit_triggers: a claim conversation reveals an expectation the record does not cover
an obligor changes the contract wording so prior expectation records no longer describe the current product
a cohort of accounts from one origin channel shows repeated surprise at the same term

base.update_signal: claim conversations repeatedly surface expectations the sale record does not account for

nodes.definition: Understand, as a mechanism rather than a number, how money reaches the agent on a contract that stays in force. The components are: whether the obligor pays renewal-side compensation at all or treats renewals as house business; whether it is a share of the renewal contract price or a flat schedule, and whether that share differs from new business; who is recorded as agent of record and how that record moves on transfer, on appointment termination, or under house-account rules; when compensation is earned versus paid, and the chargeback window that reverses it on early cancellation, refund or non-payment; whether direct-billed auto-renewals credit the writing agent indefinitely, for a limited number of terms, or not at all; and how tier changes, downgrades and obligor repricing move the base the schedule applies to. None of this is remembered or assumed: each component is read from the current representative agreement and compensation schedule and confirmed in writing with the obligor per product, because obligors differ and schedules change at their own renewal. Knowing the mechanism precisely is what makes honest non-renewal advice affordable to give, because the agent knows exactly what it costs and can decide it on the client's facts anyway.

included: the mechanism components and their drivers
agent-of-record movement, orphaning and house-account rules
chargeback windows and the per-obligor written verification path
excluded: stating any specific rate, percentage, multiple or amount as a fact
new-business commission design and channel economics, which belong to the distribution knowledge base
the agent's own tax and accounting treatment

pros.claim: Knowing the chargeback window before acting prevents a save that costs more than it earns
pros.example: a cancellation processed inside the reversal window turns a renewal into a debit, which changes whether a mid-term downgrade or a clean lapse is the better recommendation

cons.claim: Compensation literacy pulls attention to the agent's economics at exactly the moment the client needs advocacy
cons.example: an agent who computes their own downside before hearing what the client's failed system actually is

failure_modes: assuming the new-business schedule also governs renewals
discovering orphaning rules only after an appointment lapses and the book stops paying
quoting a remembered percentage to a referral partner instead of reading the current schedule
acceptance_tests: for each carried product the renewal-side schedule, agent-of-record rule, chargeback window and direct-bill crediting rule are documented from the current agreement with a date and a named obligor contact
no compensation figure is stated to a client, partner or in training material as a general fact rather than a per-agreement term
revisit_triggers: an obligor issues a new compensation schedule or amends the representative agreement
an appointment, territory or product authorization changes
a chargeback lands that the recorded window did not predict

base.update_signal: a reissued compensation schedule, an agent-of-record rule change, or an unexpected reversal on a cancelled account

nodes.definition: Hold an accurate map, per obligor carried, of what actually happens between a homeowner's failure and a resolved claim, including where the process predictably stalls. The stages are typically: the client opens the claim through the administrator's stated intake channel; a network contractor is assigned or an out-of-network one is authorized; the contractor diagnoses and reports the failure and its cause; the administrator authorizes repair, replacement or cash in lieu, requests more information, or declines; parts are ordered and the work completed; the client pays the trade service fee and any non-covered charges directly to the contractor. Stalls cluster at named points: intake outside business hours, no network contractor available in the area or trade, diagnosis reports sitting unread, parts backorders, and authorization decisions waiting on maintenance evidence. The map records for each obligor the intake channel and hours, the emergency-handling rule, the escalation stages and how each is reached, the turnaround expectations the obligor itself documents, and the stage at which agent intervention is useful rather than noise. Without this map the agent's help during a claim is limited to sympathy and guessing.

included: per-obligor stage map with intake, dispatch, diagnosis, authorization and completion
the recurring stall points and the escalation stages that address each
where agent intervention changes the outcome
excluded: performing, authorizing or paying for repairs
the obligor internal adjudication criteria
predicting the outcome of any specific claim

pros.claim: Knowing which stage a claim is stuck at converts a vague complaint into a specific, answerable ask
pros.example: telling the escalation desk that the diagnosis report was submitted four business days ago and asking for the authorization decision, rather than asking how it is going

cons.claim: The map ages badly when an obligor changes administrator or contractor network, and a stale map produces confidently wrong instructions
cons.example: sending a client to an intake number that was retired at the last administrator transition

failure_modes: one generic mental model applied to obligors whose processes differ materially
escalating at a stage where escalation does nothing and burning credibility
never recording the documented turnaround expectations, so no stall can be named as a stall
acceptance_tests: each carried obligor has a written stage map with intake channel and hours, emergency rule, escalation stages and documented turnaround expectations
each mapped stall point names the evidence or contact that unblocks it and the stage at which the agent acts
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes administrator, contractor network or intake channel
claims on one obligor begin stalling at a stage the map does not show
an escalation contact class stops responding

base.update_signal: an administrator or network transition, or a run of claims stalling at an unmapped stage

nodes.definition: Run the first call from a client whose system has just failed as a fixed sequence, because most of what the relationship becomes is decided in those ten minutes. The sequence: check safety and habitability first - no heat in a freeze, water intrusion, a gas smell, an elderly household - and say plainly when a situation needs an emergency trade call regardless of what the contract does; pull the contract and the expectation record before offering any view; confirm the plan is in force and paid and whether any waiting period touches this failure date; tell the client the exact intake channel and what the administrator will ask for, which is typically the failure date, the symptom, the system make, model and age, and any maintenance evidence; state the trade service fee they will owe when a contractor is dispatched; and close with the charter sentence that the obligor decides coverage and the agent will not guess it. The agent logs the call the same day with the failure date exactly as the client reported it and never edits that date afterwards. Coverage optimism at this moment is the single most expensive habit in this vertical, because it is remembered word for word.

included: safety and habitability triage
in-force, payment and waiting-period verification
intake instructions, evidence checklist, service-fee statement and the dated call log
excluded: deciding or predicting coverage
contacting a contractor on the client's behalf before an intake exists
advising on repair technique or diagnosing the failure

pros.claim: An accurate first call removes the two decline causes that are actually within anyone's control, late intake and missing information
pros.example: having the client gather the model plate, the serial and the last service receipt before they call intake, so diagnosis is not waiting on documents a week later

cons.claim: The honest script feels cold to a homeowner standing in a cold house, and a competitor's reassurance sounds better in the moment
cons.example: a client who wanted do not worry it is covered and got a process description instead, and says so in a review

failure_modes: promising coverage to calm a distressed client
letting the client delay intake because the agent said they would look into it first
skipping the safety question and leaving a household without heat over a weekend
acceptance_tests: the call log for every first-notice contact shows the safety check, the in-force and waiting-period check, the intake instruction, the stated service fee and the who-decides sentence
the client-reported failure date is recorded once, dated, and never amended in the file
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes intake requirements or the evidence requested at first notice
a decline is traced to information the triage sequence should have collected
an emergency-handling rule changes for a carried product

base.update_signal: a decline or delay traced back to something the first call failed to collect or told the client incorrectly

nodes.definition: Draw and hold the line between advocacy that is legitimate and pressure that is misrepresentation, and keep it visible under emotional load. Legitimate: reading the contract clause by clause with the client, asking the administrator which clause is being applied and why, chasing an authorization that has passed the obligor's own documented turnaround, supplying maintenance or installation records the client already holds, requesting a second diagnosis when the first is internally inconsistent or the contractor never inspected the failed component, insisting on the decline in writing, escalating through the obligor's stated stages, and telling the client which external complaint route exists for service contracts as a class with verify current rules in your jurisdiction attached. Illegitimate: coaching a client on what failure date or cause to report, assembling a maintenance history that was not kept, describing a claim to the administrator in terms the client never used, implying to the client that the agent can obtain a result the agent cannot deliver, or trading on a personal relationship at the escalation desk to get a claim paid that the contract does not cover. The distinction is not squeamishness: a claim built on a coached story collapses under the obligor's own investigation and takes the client's payout, the agent's appointment and the agent's escalation credibility with it.

included: the legitimate advocacy list and the prohibited list
escalation etiquette and the finite credibility budget
handling of client-held evidence
excluded: adjudicating the claim
acting as the client's legal representative
personalized legal advice about a dispute with the obligor

pros.claim: Staying inside the line keeps the agent credible at the escalation desk, which is the only currency escalation actually runs on
pros.example: an escalation contact who takes the agent's call first because the agent has never sent a reconstructed maintenance story

cons.claim: Refusing to shade the facts sometimes means watching a sympathetic client lose a claim a looser agent would have won for them
cons.example: a compressor that failed two days inside the waiting period, where the client asks the agent to describe the timing differently

failure_modes: letting sympathy drift into coaching the client's account of the failure
escalating on volume and tone rather than on evidence and dispute class
criticising the obligor to the client while continuing to sell its product
acceptance_tests: the legitimate and prohibited lists exist in writing and every escalation file shows only client-held or obligor-held evidence
no claim file contains a failure date, cause or description that differs from what the client first reported
revisit_triggers: a client asks the agent to alter a reported fact
an obligor changes its evidence or escalation requirements
an escalation is refused on credibility rather than on the merits

base.update_signal: an obligor investigation, appointment action or client complaint that turns on how a claim was represented

nodes.definition: Keep a client with a claim in progress informed on a promised cadence, in writing, whether or not there is news. The unit of work is: a contact rhythm agreed on the first call (for example an update by the end of the next business day, then at a stated interval until resolution); a short written summary after every substantive contact naming what was asked, who said what, and what happens next; and a plain statement of which stage of the lifecycle map the claim is currently at. Silence is what converts a slow claim into a public complaint - clients tolerate delay far better than they tolerate not knowing, and an agent who goes quiet is assumed to have given up or to be hiding a decline. The written summaries do double duty as the escalation file: when a claim needs escalation, the dated record of contacts, names and unanswered requests is already assembled and no reconstruction is needed. The tone rule is that the agent reports the obligor's position without endorsing it as fair or trashing it as outrageous, because both distortions come back at the client's expense.

included: the agreed cadence and no-news updates
written summaries naming contacts, requests and next steps
stage reporting and escalation-file assembly
excluded: authorizing work or committing the obligor to a timeline it has not given
sharing another client's claim experience
characterising a pending decision as decided

pros.claim: A documented cadence turns a stalled claim into an escalation with dates attached rather than a complaint with adjectives
pros.example: a summary trail showing the same authorization request unanswered across three logged contacts over eight business days

cons.claim: Cadence costs real hours on claims the agent earns nothing extra to handle, and heavy claim seasons collide with renewal work
cons.example: a mid-winter heating wave where daily updates crowd out the renewal calendar for the same weeks

failure_modes: updating only when there is news, so silence signals bad news
verbal-only updates that leave nothing to escalate with
editorialising about the obligor in a written summary that later travels
acceptance_tests: every open claim shows a contact within the promised interval and a written summary after each substantive contact
each open claim file names its current lifecycle stage and the next dated action with an owner
revisit_triggers: a claim exceeds the promised cadence without an update
claim volume makes the promised cadence unachievable across the book
a client complains about not knowing rather than about the outcome

base.update_signal: complaint themes or exit interviews that cite silence during a claim rather than the claim outcome

nodes.definition: Turn a decline into a classified, checkable object instead of a verdict. First obtain the reason in writing and identify which clause class was applied: pre-existing condition, lack of or improper maintenance, improper installation or unpermitted modification, code or permit upgrade, a non-covered component inside a covered system, secondary or consequential damage, cap or aggregate limit exhaustion, waiting-period timing, or plan not in force. Then classify the dispute type, because the clause alone does not tell the agent what to do: factual, where the obligor believes something about the failure that the evidence contradicts; documentary, where the client can supply what is missing; interpretive, where both sides read the same clause differently; or correct, where the contract plainly excludes this and the answer will not change however hard anyone pushes. Each class has a different next move and a different honest expectation to set with the client, and the fourth class is the one agents avoid naming and clients most need to hear early. Decoding also feeds the obligor performance record: one pre-existing-condition decline is a claim, a cluster of them across unrelated homes is a signal about the product or the inspection standard behind it.

included: obtaining the written rationale
clause-class identification and dispute-type classification
feeding the classified outcome into the per-obligor record
excluded: first-principles interpretation of the clause wording, which the coverage-terms knowledge base owns
asserting what the obligor will ultimately pay
opinions on the legal enforceability of a clause

pros.claim: Classification tells the client within one conversation whether to gather documents, wait, or accept, instead of leaving them to hope indefinitely
pros.example: a maintenance-documentation decline that the client's dated service receipts resolve, versus a plainly excluded item where further effort is only cruelty

cons.claim: Naming a decline correct and final costs the agent the client's hope and often the renewal, in the same call
cons.example: telling a homeowner that their roof leak was never covered under this plan and hearing that the whole product is therefore worthless

failure_modes: accepting a verbal reason and never getting the clause in writing
treating every decline as contestable, which trains clients to expect reversals that will not come
reading a cluster of one decline class as a run of unlucky clients rather than as a product signal
acceptance_tests: every decline in the book has a written rationale on file, a clause class and a dispute type recorded
declines classified as correct and final are communicated as such to the client within the promised cadence, with the reason in plain language
revisit_triggers: a clause class starts appearing across unrelated homes on one obligor
an obligor changes contract wording or its inspection and maintenance evidence standard
a decline class the agent recorded as correct is reversed on escalation

base.update_signal: a shift in the mix of clause classes across the book, or an obligor restating its evidence standard for a class

nodes.definition: Run a fixed sequence after a decline so the response is proportionate to the dispute class and never improvised in front of an upset client. The sequence: confirm the written rationale exists and is specific enough to act on; re-read the cited clause with the client and say plainly whether the wording supports the obligor; assemble the evidence class that could move a factual or documentary decline, which is typically dated service records, installation or permit records, inspection reports, photographs, and where the client chooses to fund one, an independent diagnosis; submit it once, complete, through the stated channel with a dated cover summary rather than drip-feeding; escalate to the next named stage if the response is silence or a non-answer rather than a reasoned position; tell the client which external complaint route exists for service contracts where they live and that using it is their right, naming it as a class with verify current rules in your jurisdiction; and where the decline is correct under the contract, say so, explain what would have covered it, and move the conversation to what the client is actually going to do about the broken system. The playbook always ends in a decision, never in an open loop the client is left holding.

included: evidence assembly and one complete submission
escalation staging matched to dispute class
the honest acceptance path and closing the loop with a decision
excluded: representing the client in a legal or regulatory proceeding
guaranteeing any outcome
paying, offsetting or discounting a declined claim personally to keep the account

pros.claim: One complete resubmission beats five partial ones and materially shortens the cycle
pros.example: sending the dated service records, the installation date and the independent diagnosis together with a cover summary rather than as three separate emails over two weeks

cons.claim: Escalation spends a finite credibility budget, and spending it on a plainly excluded claim weakens the next case that deserved it
cons.example: a formal complaint filed over a cap-exhaustion decline that was arithmetically correct on the face of the contract

failure_modes: appealing indiscriminately so that the escalation desk stops distinguishing this agent's real cases
leaving the client to escalate alone after the first no
letting frustration with the obligor become public criticism while still selling its product
acceptance_tests: each contested decline shows a single complete evidence submission with a dated cover summary and a named recipient
each closed decline shows a recorded end state: reversed, partially resolved, escalated to a named external route, or accepted as correct with the client told why
revisit_triggers: an escalation stage stops producing reasoned responses
a class of decline starts reversing on evidence the playbook does not currently collect
an obligor changes its complaint process or evidence requirements

base.update_signal: the reversal rate by dispute class shifts, or an obligor changes what evidence it will reconsider on

nodes.definition: Help the client evaluate the outcomes that are neither a clean repair nor a decline, which is where most of this product's dissatisfaction actually lives. These include a cash-in-lieu offer instead of replacement, an authorization limited by a per-system or aggregate cap, a repair authorized where the client expected replacement, a replacement of like kind and quality where the failed unit was better than a current base model, and the non-covered adjacent costs that arrive attached to a covered replacement - code and permit upgrades, disposal, refrigerant or line-set work, electrical or duct modifications, access and crane charges, and efficiency upgrades the client wants. The agent's job is to lay out what the offer covers, what the client will still pay out of pocket, what accepting forecloses, and how the contract describes the valuation basis the obligor used, so the client decides with the real arithmetic in front of them rather than discovering it from a contractor a week later. The agent does not tell the client what to accept, does not appraise equipment, and does not produce a replacement quote as though they were the contractor.

included: explaining the offer structure and the contract valuation basis
surfacing non-covered adjacent costs before acceptance
comparing accept against continue and naming what acceptance closes off
excluded: negotiating a settlement as the client's representative
appraising equipment or quoting replacement cost
personalized financial advice about whether to spend the money

pros.claim: Naming the adjacent costs before acceptance prevents the worst renewal conversation in the business
pros.example: a client who accepts a cash offer, then meets permit, disposal and line-set costs nobody mentioned, and concludes both the plan and the agent misled them

cons.claim: Laying the gaps out invites the client to conclude the product underdelivers, at exactly the moment their renewal decision is near
cons.example: a capped compressor payout that visibly falls short of what an installed system costs in their market

failure_modes: letting the client accept cash in lieu without the adjacent-cost conversation
arguing the valuation with the administrator on the client's behalf as though the agent could set it
treating a capped outcome as a decline and escalating a claim that was actually paid to its limit
acceptance_tests: every partial or cash-in-lieu outcome file records the offer, the contract valuation basis cited, the adjacent costs named to the client, and the client's decision
no file shows the agent quoting a replacement price or recommending acceptance as advice
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes its cash-in-lieu valuation basis or its like-kind standard
clients repeatedly report adjacent costs the checklist does not include
cap exhaustion starts arriving earlier in the term across a cohort

base.update_signal: client-reported out-of-pocket costs after acceptance that the adjacent-cost checklist did not anticipate

nodes.definition: Run renewals from a calendar built out of each contract's own mechanics rather than from a monthly mailing. Per account the calendar carries the expiry or anniversary date, whether the term renews automatically or must be actively renewed, the notice window in which the obligor must send and the client may act on a rate or term change, the payment instrument and its expiry date, the cancellation and refund windows that attach, and the client's consent status and preferred channel. From those it sets touches: a pre-renewal review contact placed early enough that the client can still act before an auto-renew charge lands, a post-claim check for accounts that had a claim during the term, and a confirmation after the renewal processes. The calendar also flags accounts where a touch is constrained - consent withdrawn, an obligor-owned direct-bill relationship, a property that has changed hands - so the agent does not contact where they should not. Renewal work that begins when the invoice lands has already lost the only window in which the client had a real choice, and that lost window is what most auto-renew complaints are actually about.

included: per-account timing fields and notice windows
the touch schedule and its placement before auto-renew charges
consent-constrained and direct-bill accounts flagged out of campaigns
excluded: the content of the value or rate conversation, which are their own units
obligor billing operations
asserting a jurisdiction's specific notice, consent or auto-renew rules

pros.claim: Contacting before the auto-renew charge converts a surprise into a decision the client made
pros.example: reaching a client two weeks before the stored card is charged at a changed rate, instead of after they have already disputed it with their bank

cons.claim: A calendar is only as good as its worst field, and stale payment or consent data produces contacts that cost more than they retain
cons.example: an auto-renew reminder sent to a client who withdrew contact consent after a bad claim

failure_modes: one uniform renewal window applied to products whose notice mechanics differ
treating auto-renewal as a reason not to contact at all
campaigning to consent-withdrawn or transferred accounts because the calendar was built from sale dates alone
acceptance_tests: every in-force account has a renewal date, renewal mechanism, notice window, payment expiry and consent status populated and a scheduled pre-renewal touch
no scheduled touch targets an account flagged consent-withdrawn, transferred or obligor-direct
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes its renewal, notice or auto-renew mechanics
a cohort begins lapsing at auto-renew rather than at an active decision
contact-consent obligations change for a served jurisdiction

base.update_signal: an obligor notice or auto-renew mechanic change, or a rise in lapses that happen silently at auto-renew

nodes.definition: Decide, per account and before any renewal conversation, whether this plan is still worth what this client will pay for it. The test assembles four inputs. The home's remaining covered risk: which systems are still original, their age against typical service life, what has been replaced during the term and whether that replacement carries a manufacturer warranty that now duplicates the plan. The account's own history: claims authorized, trade service fees paid, caps consumed, declines and their clause classes, and whether the recurring decline class will recur again next term. The coming terms: the price, service fee, caps, tier definitions and exclusions as the obligor has now set them. And the client's position: their tolerance for a large unplanned repair bill, whether they have a maintenance-capable contractor relationship of their own, whether they are selling, and whether their circumstances have changed. The output is one of four recommendations with a written reason - renew as is, renew at a different tier, renew with a different obligor, or do not renew - and the reason is recorded before the agent looks at what any of those outcomes pays them. The honest alternative that the test must always include is the client self-funding the same risk.

included: remaining covered risk inventory and duplicate-coverage check
account claim and decline history with cap consumption
the changed terms and the client position
a four-way recommendation with a recorded reason
excluded: tier-to-home matching at first sale, which the coverage-terms knowledge base owns
personalized financial advice about the client's savings or budget
predicting future claim outcomes or quoting savings figures

pros.claim: A written test makes the recommendation defensible whichever way it lands, to the client and to the obligor
pros.example: a file showing the renew-at-lower-tier reason was recorded before the compensation consequence of that tier was looked up

cons.claim: The test can only use the risk facts the agent has, and homeowners under-report system ages and prior work
cons.example: a furnace the client believed a previous owner had replaced, which turns out to be original to the house

failure_modes: running the test only on accounts the agent expects to keep
reading a claim-free term as proof the plan was worthless, or a claim-heavy term as proof it is priceless, instead of pricing the remaining risk
letting the compensation schedule pick the recommendation and writing the reason afterwards
acceptance_tests: every account reaching its renewal window has a dated test with all four inputs recorded and one of the four recommendations with a written reason
the recorded reason references the home's remaining covered risk and the account's own claim history, not the agent's compensation
revisit_triggers: the obligor reprices, retiers or rewrites exclusions for the coming term
a covered system is replaced mid-term or comes under a manufacturer warranty
the client's circumstances change materially, including a decision to sell

base.update_signal: renewal outcomes and later claim experience showing the test systematically over- or under-recommends renewal for a home profile

nodes.definition: Present a changed renewal openly, including the parts that are worse for this client. Obligors reprice and re-paper renewals: the contract price moves, the trade service fee moves, per-system and aggregate caps are re-set, individual systems and appliances move between tiers, exclusions are added or broadened, and the term or auto-renew mechanics change. The conversation names each change against the terms the client had last term, states which direction each moves for this particular home, and explains the mechanism behind the change where the obligor has actually given one - claims experience across its book, contractor and parts cost movement, a tier redesign - without inventing a figure or a justification the obligor never offered. The delta is never buried in a re-sent brochure or a link. Where a change materially reduces value for this home, the agent says so in the same breath as the value test's recommendation, which may be to move tier, move obligor or not renew at all. Clients forgive an increase they were told about far more readily than a smaller one they discover on a statement, and the discovered one is what generates the complaint.

included: change-by-change comparison against the prior term
direction of impact for this specific home
the obligor's stated mechanism where one exists, and pairing with the value-test recommendation
excluded: negotiating obligor pricing, which the agent cannot do
asserting the obligor's internal pricing rationale as fact
quoting amounts, percentages or market averages as general facts

pros.claim: A side-by-side of last term against this term makes the agent the source of the bad news rather than the billing statement
pros.example: naming a raised trade service fee and a re-set per-system cap in the same call as the recommendation to move down a tier

cons.claim: Full disclosure of a worsened renewal loses accounts that silence would have carried for one more term
cons.example: a client who lapses on hearing that their pool equipment moved out of the tier they had been buying

failure_modes: sending the renewal packet and calling that disclosure
explaining an increase with an invented cost story the obligor never stated
disclosing the price change but not the cap, tier or exclusion changes that matter more
acceptance_tests: each renewal conversation record shows every changed term named against the prior term with its direction of impact for this client
no renewal record contains a pricing rationale attributed to the obligor that the obligor did not state
revisit_triggers: an obligor issues new renewal terms, tier definitions or caps
clients report being surprised by a term at first claim after renewal
a renewal cohort lapses immediately after the first billing statement

base.update_signal: post-renewal complaints or first-claim surprises showing a changed term was not actually communicated

nodes.definition: Tell a client the plan is not worth renewing when the value test says so, and do it in a way they can act on. The cases recur and are recognisable: the home's covered systems have all been replaced recently and carry manufacturer coverage that duplicates the plan; the client has the cash buffer and the contractor relationships to absorb the failures the plan would cover, and prefers to; repeated declines in a class that will recur - an unmaintainable system, an excluded modification, a chronic pre-existing finding - mean this plan cannot pay for this home's real risk; the renewal price and trade service fee together now sit close to the client's realistic annual repair exposure; or the client is selling, and a transfer or a listing-side arrangement fits better than a renewal. The advice states what the client is taking on, what would make a plan worth revisiting later, and an offer to review again next year, and it is recorded in the file with its reason. This unit is what makes the rest of the book trustworthy, and it is the one the compensation mechanics argue against, which is exactly why it is written as a rule rather than left as a mood.

included: the recurring do-not-renew cases
how the advice is delivered, what it must include, and how it is recorded
the standing offer to review again later
excluded: telling the client what to do with the money they save, which is personalized financial advice
disparaging the obligor
asserting that the client will or will not have a failure

pros.claim: The advice is remembered and referred on long past the lost renewal
pros.example: a client told not to renew who sends a neighbour and returns as a buyer at their next home purchase

cons.claim: It is an immediate and direct cost to the book that cannot be justified inside a single renewal cycle
cons.example: a persistency figure that trails a peer who renewed every account without running a test

failure_modes: never giving the advice, so the book quietly fills with accounts that should have lapsed
giving it as a throwaway line with no recorded reason and no revisit offer
using it to shed service-heavy accounts rather than because the value test failed
acceptance_tests: every do-not-renew recommendation is delivered with the reason, what the client is taking on, and a revisit offer, and is recorded in the file
the rate of do-not-renew advice is reported in the book review rather than left invisible
revisit_triggers: an obligor materially improves or worsens the terms that drove a prior do-not-renew recommendation
a client who was advised not to renew reports a large failure the plan would have covered
the do-not-renew rate moves sharply in either direction

base.update_signal: outcomes for clients advised not to renew, and whether their later repair experience matched the advice

nodes.definition: Keep an explicit written inventory of what the agent may legitimately do to keep an account, separated from what this vertical's worst practitioners do, because retention pressure peaks exactly when the honest answer is weakest. Legitimate levers act on fit and clarity: correcting a tier that never matched the home; adding or dropping optional coverage the client does or does not need; trading a higher trade service fee for a lower contract price or the reverse where the obligor offers that choice; moving the account to a different obligor whose claim performance suits this home better; changing payment frequency or instrument; resolving an open claim before the renewal date so the decision is made on a settled experience; and re-running the expectation conversation that was rushed at a closing table. Prohibited levers act on fear and friction: warning of catastrophic failures with no basis in this home's condition, implying coverage the contract does not contain, leaning on the auto-renew to carry a client who has not been told about a change, and making cancellation harder than renewal. A written lever list is what an agent reaches for under quota pressure, and its absence is what a scare story fills.

included: the legitimate lever list and when each applies
the prohibited practice list
the rule that a lever must address the reason the client actually gave
excluded: fear-based or urgency-manufactured selling in any form
new-business offer design, which belongs to the distribution knowledge base
changing contract terms, which only the obligor can do

pros.claim: A fixed lever list keeps retention work honest when a shortfall is visible and the quarter is closing
pros.example: an agent facing a renewal gap reaching for a tier correction on a home whose systems changed, rather than a story about the client's aging furnace

cons.claim: Honest levers convert fewer saves than fear does, and the shortfall shows up this quarter while the trust shows up over years
cons.example: a save rate that trails a competitor who sells catastrophe at every renewal call

failure_modes: reaching for a lever that does not address the reason the client gave
stacking discounts and coverage changes until the client no longer understands what they hold
letting the prohibited list exist in training but not in the actual save call
acceptance_tests: every save attempt records the client's stated reason and the lever applied, and the lever addresses that reason
no save record contains a claim about the home's condition or future failures that is not evidenced by the account file or the client's own report
revisit_triggers: an obligor adds or removes a tier, fee option or payment option that changes the lever set
save-call reviews find a lever applied that did not match the stated reason
a save is followed within one term by a complaint or a decline the save conversation implied would be covered

base.update_signal: save-call review or complaint themes showing a lever being used as pressure rather than as a fit correction

nodes.definition: Handle a request to cancel as a request to cancel. The mechanics the agent must know per product, read from the current contract and obligor procedure rather than remembered: the right-to-cancel or free-look class that the contract and the jurisdiction attach to the sale; whether refunds are computed pro rata or on a short-rate basis and what administrative charge applies; whether claims already authorized offset a refund; who actually processes the cancellation, which may be the obligor, the administrator or a third-party biller, and what the client must submit and to whom; what happens to a stored auto-renew authorization and how the client confirms it is revoked; and what chargeback exposure the cancellation creates for the agent. The conduct rule sits above all of it: the agent states the cancellation path clearly and does not gate it behind a retention conversation. One honest alternative may be offered once, briefly, and only where it genuinely addresses the reason the client gave; if the client repeats the request, the agent processes it and confirms in writing the same day. Obstruction is both the practice this product class is scrutinised for hardest and the fastest way to turn a quiet departure into a public complaint.

included: per-product cancellation and refund mechanics and who processes them
the offer-once rule and same-day written confirmation
auto-renew authorization revocation and agent chargeback awareness
excluded: asserting a jurisdiction's specific cancellation, free-look or refund rules, which must be verified with the applicable regulator and the obligor
processing or funding a refund the obligor owes
any script that delays, conditions or complicates a stated cancellation

pros.claim: A clean cancellation preserves both the referral relationship and the possibility of a later sale
pros.example: a client who cancels because they are selling the home and returns as a buyer at their next purchase

cons.claim: Frictionless cancellation surrenders accounts a longer conversation might have kept, and the chargeback lands on the agent regardless
cons.example: a mid-term cancellation inside the reversal window on business written earlier the same year

failure_modes: routing a cancellation request into a save queue instead of processing it
telling a client the refund basis from memory and being wrong about the administrative charge
leaving a stored auto-renew authorization live after a cancellation is agreed
acceptance_tests: every cancellation request shows the stated path given, at most one alternative offered, and written confirmation issued the same day the client repeated the request
each carried product has its cancellation processor, refund basis and auto-renew revocation step documented from current obligor procedure with a date
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes its cancellation, refund or auto-renew revocation procedure
a cancellation-related complaint or chargeback dispute arises
cancellation or free-look obligation classes change in a served jurisdiction

base.update_signal: a cancellation complaint, a disputed refund basis, or an obligor procedure change for cancellations and auto-renew revocation

nodes.definition: Apply heightened care where the client is elderly, recently bereaved, cognitively impaired, isolated, or in financial distress, because this product's renewal and claim mechanics can harm those clients specifically and quietly. The practices: never let an auto-renew carry an account whose holder may not understand that it is renewing; confirm comprehension at renewal in the client's own words rather than accepting a yes; slow the pace and offer to include a family member, caregiver or other trusted contact where the client agrees to it; check that the payment instrument belongs to the client and that the plan is not being carried past their means; refuse to sell an upgrade or an additional plan during an active claim crisis, when the client will agree to anything to get their heat back; treat repeated confusion about what is covered as a signal to review whether the plan should continue at all rather than as a sales opportunity; and route suspected financial exploitation to the obligor's reporting channel and the reporting route class that applies where the client lives, rather than handling it privately. The plan's cost is small next to a home repair, and that is exactly what makes years of silent renewals on a vulnerable client easy to overlook and impossible to defend once found.

included: comprehension confirmation in the client's own words
restraint on auto-renew reliance and on upgrades during a crisis
consented trusted-contact practice and escalation of suspected exploitation as a class
excluded: diagnosing capacity or making a capacity determination
acting as a fiduciary, attorney-in-fact or caregiver
asserting a jurisdiction's specific reporting or vulnerable-adult requirements

pros.claim: The practice prevents the failure this product class is criticised for most and defended for least
pros.example: a plan that renewed silently for years on an elderly client who no longer knew it existed and never filed a claim

cons.claim: Comprehension checks lengthen every renewal and can read as patronising to sharp older clients
cons.example: a client who resents being asked to explain their own plan back before it will be renewed

failure_modes: accepting a yes as comprehension because the call is long and the day is full
selling an upgrade during a heating failure to a distressed client
involving a family member without the client's consent, which is its own breach
acceptance_tests: renewal records for flagged accounts show comprehension confirmed in the client's own words and an active renewal decision rather than an auto-renew default
no upgrade or additional plan is recorded as sold to a flagged client during an open claim, and any trusted-contact involvement shows recorded client consent
revisit_triggers: a client shows repeated confusion about coverage across contacts
a family member or caregiver raises a concern about an account
vulnerable-adult or exploitation reporting obligation classes change in a served jurisdiction

base.update_signal: a complaint, family enquiry or internal review involving a client who did not understand a renewal they were paying for

nodes.definition: Model where reputation damage in this business actually originates and which part of it the agent owns, because the instinct to treat every bad review as either the obligor's fault or the client's unreasonableness prevents the only fixes that work. The product class generates public complaints structurally: coverage is defined and partial, failures are urgent and expensive, the obligor decides, and the only person the client can reach is the agent. Separate three streams. Complaints about the product: a decline the contract plainly supports, where the damage comes from what the buyer believed rather than from what happened. Complaints about the obligor's service: slow dispatch, an unavailable network, poor contractor work, unanswered escalations. Complaints about the agent: an expectation oversold, a call not returned, a renewal change not disclosed. Only the third is fully the agent's to prevent, but all three arrive attached to the agent's name, and the second is chosen by the agent every time they decide which obligor to sell. The model also names the leading indicators available before a review appears - claims stalled past cadence, one decline class clustering, referral partners going quiet, renewal calls where the client is surprised by a term - because reputation in this vertical is managed at the point of sale and the point of decline, not on review sites.

included: the three complaint streams and who owns each
leading indicators watchable before a public complaint
where prevention actually happens in the sale and claim path
excluded: soliciting, incentivising or fabricating reviews
suppressing or burying legitimate complaints
defending the obligor's claim decisions in public

pros.claim: Separating the streams stops the agent both from absorbing blame for the contract and from dodging blame for their own selling
pros.example: a decline complaint traced to a tier the agent recommended without walking the exclusions, which is an agent-conduct fix and not a product fix

cons.claim: The model gives the agent no control over the largest stream, so an obligor's bad quarter damages an agent who did everything right
cons.example: an administrator transition that lengthens dispatch times across an entire book at once

failure_modes: counting only public reviews and missing the private churn that precedes them
attributing every complaint to the product to avoid examining the sale
watching lagging indicators only, so the first signal is a review
acceptance_tests: complaints and negative signals are recorded against one of the three streams with the evidence for that attribution
the leading indicators are reviewed on a stated cadence and each has a named threshold that triggers action
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes administrator or contractor network
a leading indicator crosses its threshold
complaint volume rises in a cohort without a change in claim volume

base.update_signal: a shift in the attribution mix across streams, or a leading indicator that reliably precedes public complaints

nodes.definition: Answer a public complaint without breaching the client's privacy, arguing the claim in public, or pretending the product is something it is not. The standing pattern: respond quickly and disclose nothing - no account details, no property, no system, no dates, no diagnosis, no decision; state that an individual's contract cannot be discussed publicly; give a direct channel and a named person to continue offline; and follow through there the same day. Where the complaint concerns a decline the contract supports, the offline conversation explains the clause plainly and offers the obligor's escalation stages and the external complaint route as classes rather than debating the merits in a public thread. Where the complaint concerns the agent's own conduct - a call not returned, a change not disclosed - the correct move is an apology and a concrete fix, made publicly if the criticism was public. Never post claim facts to win an argument, never imply that a client is lying, never offer a benefit in exchange for removing a review, and never phrase a reply in a way that could be read as a coverage determination the agent has no authority to make. Complaints filed with a regulator or the obligor's compliance function follow that body's process, not this one.

included: the no-detail public reply pattern and same-day offline continuation
apology and fix for agent-conduct complaints
pointing to escalation and external complaint routes as classes
excluded: incentivised, solicited-under-pressure or fabricated reviews and any benefit offered for removal
disclosing any client, property or claim detail publicly
formal regulator or obligor compliance responses, which follow their own process

pros.claim: A disciplined reply protects the client's privacy and the agent's credibility at the same time
pros.example: a public reply that names nothing, moves the discussion offline within hours, and is followed by a same-day call

cons.claim: A restrained reply reads as evasive to onlookers who wanted the agent's side of it, and unrebutted damage is real damage
cons.example: a detailed but inaccurate review that stands on the public record because the accurate answer would require disclosing the claim

failure_modes: correcting the client's facts in public and turning a complaint into a privacy incident
silence, which reads as confirmation
offering a discount or benefit in exchange for taking a review down
acceptance_tests: every public reply contains no account, property, claim or decision detail and gives a named offline contact
each public complaint has a logged same-day offline follow-up and a recorded outcome, including any agent-conduct fix made
revisit_triggers: a complaint alleges conduct rather than product or service
a platform or obligor changes what an appointed representative may say publicly
the same complaint theme appears from more than one client

base.update_signal: a public reply that drew a privacy, advertising or compliance objection, or a recurring complaint theme naming agent conduct

nodes.definition: Manage the referral relationship as a post-sale system, because in this vertical one declined claim at one closing can end a stream of business. Listing and buyer agents, brokerages, property managers and trade contractors hand clients over on the strength of their own reputation, and they hear about a bad claim before the agent does. The work has four parts. Brief the partner on what the product does and does not do, in the same plain terms used with homeowners, so the partner never sells it onward as full-coverage insurance on the agent's behalf. Agree in advance what happens when a claim is declined: who the client calls, what the agent will do, and within what time. Close the loop by telling the partner when one of their referrals has had a bad experience - with the client's consent and without claim detail the client has not authorised - rather than letting them hear it only from an angry client months later. And treat a partner who pressures the agent to gloss the exclusions at the closing table as a channel risk to be re-briefed or exited, not merely as a difficult personality. This unit is the post-sale half of the referral relationship; the channel's economics and compliance class belong to the distribution knowledge base.

included: partner briefing on the product's real limits
the pre-agreed decline-handling protocol with the partner
consented feedback to the partner and treating gloss-pressure as a channel risk
excluded: referral compensation structures, channel economics and per-channel compliance classes
sharing client or claim detail without the client's consent
promising a partner that their referrals' claims will be paid

pros.claim: A partner who understands the limits defends the product accurately when their own client is upset
pros.example: a listing agent who tells a seller up front which systems fall outside the plan and is therefore not blindsided when a claim is declined

cons.claim: Honest partner briefings cost volume with partners who want a frictionless closing gift
cons.example: a brokerage relationship that cools once exclusions are named out loud in front of clients at the table

failure_modes: letting the partner become the product's explainer without a briefing
learning about a partner's dissatisfaction only when referrals stop arriving
sharing a client's claim outcome with a partner without consent in order to defend the agent's own handling
acceptance_tests: each active referral partner has a dated briefing record covering the product's limits and the agreed decline-handling protocol
every partner feedback contact about a specific referral shows the client's recorded consent and contains no unauthorised claim detail
revisit_triggers: a partner's referral volume drops without an explanation
a partner is heard describing the plan as covering everything
a decline occurs on a referral from a partner who has no briefing on file

base.update_signal: referral volume or partner sentiment moving after a decline, or a partner found mis-describing the product

nodes.definition: Judge each obligor by what happens to this agent's own clients after the sale, on evidence the agent collected, rather than on the compensation schedule or the sales-desk story. The review assembles from the ledger, per obligor and per period: time from intake to dispatch and from diagnosis to authorization; the share of claims resolved without escalation; decline counts by clause class; contractor-quality complaints; cash-in-lieu frequency and how often clients accepted; cancellation and complaint counts; and the qualitative record of how the escalation desk actually behaved when pressed. Patterns are read against the product rather than against the clients: one pre-existing-condition decline is a claim, a cluster of them across unrelated homes is a signal about the product or the inspection standard behind it. The output is a decision with a date attached - keep selling, restrict to specific home profiles or tiers, pause new business pending a fix, or stop - and where the decision is to stop, the agent tells affected clients what it means for the contracts they already hold, which remain the obligor's to honour. This review is also the honest input to whether the agent can keep recommending renewal into that obligor at all.

included: per-obligor claim evidence assembly from the agent's own book
pattern reading against product rather than clients
the dated keep, restrict, pause or stop decision and what existing clients are told
excluded: auditing obligor finances, reserves or backing arrangements and the initial obligor diligence screen, which belong to the distribution knowledge base
publishing comparative performance claims about a named obligor
adjudicating any individual claim

pros.claim: Book evidence beats anecdote and makes a hard decision defensible to the obligor, to partners and to clients
pros.example: a documented deterioration in dispatch times beginning at an administrator transition, rather than a feeling that service got worse

cons.claim: The evidence base is small, self-selected and slow to accumulate, so a stop decision can rest on a handful of loud accounts
cons.example: three bad claims in one trade in one season reading as a systemic failure when it was a local contractor shortage

failure_modes: reviewing only when a complaint forces it, so the record is built from the worst cases
letting compensation attractiveness override documented claim performance
stopping sales on an obligor without telling existing clients what changes for them and what does not
acceptance_tests: each carried obligor has a dated review with the evidence set assembled from the ledger and one of the four decisions recorded
any pause or stop decision has a written client communication covering what happens to contracts already in force
revisit_triggers: an obligor changes administrator, network or claim staffing
a decline class or dispatch metric moves sharply for one obligor
an obligor disputes the agent's characterisation of its performance

base.update_signal: another period of claim evidence, or an obligor operational change that invalidates the prior period's metrics

nodes.definition: Review the whole in-force book on a fixed cadence and decide where to intervene, because individual renewals hide the patterns that actually decide this business.
