The review reads from the ledger: persistency by cohort, split by origin channel, obligor, tier and year written; claim incidence and the mix of outcomes across authorized, partial, cash in lieu and declined; the rate at which the value test produced do-not-renew advice and whether that rate is moving; complaint and cancellation counts by cohort; the share of accounts carrying a complete expectation record; the share of open claims that met the promised communication cadence; and the concentration of the book in any single obligor, referral partner or tier. Every finding maps to an intervention with a named owner and a date - repair expectation capture in a channel that keeps producing surprised clients, restrict or pause an obligor, rebuild the touch schedule for a cohort that lapses silently at auto-renew, re-brief or exit a partner whose referrals arrive mis-set. A book measured only by renewal count will keep renewing exactly the accounts that should have been advised to lapse, and will look healthy while its reputation erodes.

included: cohort metrics computed from the ledger
interventions with named owners and dates
concentration risk across obligor, partner and tier
excluded: forecasting revenue with invented figures or stating book value multiples
new-business production planning, which belongs to the distribution knowledge base
reviewing individual claims, which happens in the claim units

pros.claim: Cohort views expose causes that single accounts never reveal
pros.example: one origin channel producing most of the surprised-at-decline complaints, which points at how the plan is presented there rather than at the product

cons.claim: Cohort statistics on a small book are noisy and tempt overcorrection
cons.example: exiting a productive referral partner on one bad quarter driven by two unrelated equipment failures

failure_modes: measuring persistency alone and calling a quietly mis-sold book healthy
producing findings with no owner or date, so nothing changes before the next review
reacting to a single quarter's noise as though it were a trend
acceptance_tests: each review period produces cohort metrics for persistency, claim outcome mix, complaint and cancellation counts, expectation-record completeness and concentration
every finding has an intervention with a named owner and a due date, and the prior period's interventions are closed out or explicitly carried
revisit_triggers: persistency or complaint rate moves materially in any cohort
an obligor decision changes the composition of the book
the do-not-renew advice rate moves sharply in either direction

base.update_signal: a new review period's cohort metrics, or an intervention that failed to move the metric it targeted

edges.why_related: the charter defines who the agent is responsible to after the sale, which is what makes maintaining a book of those responsibilities necessary at all
the map is built to serve the guide role the charter defines, and records only the stages where that role can act
the advocacy line is the charter's promise boundary applied to the moment a claim is contested
the expectation record has to live attached to the account record or it cannot be read before a claim call
the calendar is a view over the ledger's dates, renewal mechanics, payment and consent fields
the triage script can only give correct intake instructions if the obligor's stages, channels and hours are already mapped
the agent reads what the client was told at sale before saying anything on the first call about a failure
the failure date, symptom and evidence captured at first notice are what a decline is later classified against
the response is chosen by dispute class, so nothing can be responded to before it is classified
the playbook's evidence and escalation steps are bounded by what counts as legitimate advocacy
a capped or cash-in-lieu outcome must first be distinguished from a decline before it can be evaluated as an offer
the calendar decides when the test must be run so the client still has a window to act
what the account actually received during the term, including capped and partial outcomes, is a direct input to whether the plan is worth renewing
the changed terms are presented alongside the recommendation the test produced, not on their own
do-not-renew advice is one of the four outputs of the test and is never given without it
knowing exactly what the advice costs the agent is what allows it to be given deliberately rather than avoided
a lever is only chosen after the client has heard the actual changed terms and reacted to them
cancellation handling applies the same legitimate-lever inventory under the tightest conduct constraint
attributing a complaint to the product, the obligor's service or the agent's selling requires the decline to be classified first
which stream a complaint belongs to decides whether the correct response is an explanation, an escalation route or an apology and a fix
per-obligor claim performance is one of the cohort dimensions the book review reads and acts on
the never-say list constrains the lever inventory: no lever may imply coverage the contract does not contain
edges.risk_of_conflict: quota pressure invites a lever that quietly re-promises coverage

edges.why_related: the same truthfulness and no-misrepresentation limits that bind escalation also bind what may be said in a public reply
flagged accounts constrain the calendar: they cannot be carried by an auto-renew touch and require an active, comprehension-confirmed decision
what the client was originally told bounds how a changed term may be framed, because a change cannot be described as consistent with a promise that was never made
the compensation mechanism pays for renewals and pays nothing for advising a client to lapse, so the two pull in opposite directions on every marginal account
edges.resolution_rule: the value test's recorded recommendation governs and is written before the compensation consequence is looked up; a failed value test always produces downgrade, obligor-change or do-not-renew advice, and the compensation effect is recorded as a cost, never as a reason

edges.why_related: retention work wants another conversation and the client has asked to leave, which is precisely where obstruction starts
edges.resolution_rule: a stated cancellation request is processed; one honest alternative may be offered once and only if it addresses the reason the client gave; if the client repeats the request the agent processes it and confirms in writing the same day

edges.why_related: the expectation record would often rebut an unfair public review, and publishing any of it would breach the client's confidentiality
edges.resolution_rule: confidentiality wins without exception; the record is used offline with the client, with the obligor and in a regulator or compliance process, and never in a public reply, whatever the review says

edges.why_related: a referral partner wants a frictionless closing and full limit-setting introduces friction at exactly that table
edges.resolution_rule: the homeowner's informed expectation wins; the exclusions and caps are named at the table regardless of partner preference, and a partner who requires them glossed is re-briefed and, if that fails, exited as a channel risk

edges.why_related: the obligor that pays best on the book is not necessarily the one that treats claimants best, and the evidence usually arrives after the book is already concentrated there
edges.resolution_rule: documented claim-performance evidence governs the keep, restrict, pause or stop decision and compensation is never the tiebreaker; where a stop is chosen, in-force clients are told what it means for contracts that remain the obligor's to honour

edges.why_related: expectations that were never set at sale are what later produce the public complaints the agent has to answer with one hand tied
silence during a slow claim, more than the claim outcome itself, is what converts a frustrated client into a public complainant
a decline class that will recur on this home next term is direct evidence that the plan cannot pay for this home's real risk
the update rhythm is promised during the first call and executed from that point until the claim resolves
decoding happens at a specific stage of the mapped path, after authorization is refused and before any escalation is chosen
cohort findings about surprised clients feed back into how expectations are captured and repaired for the channel that produced them
what the review learns about dispatch, escalation behaviour and stall points updates the stage map the next claim is run against
clients told honestly not to renew become the referral evidence that the agent is not merely selling contracts

both are conversations where the honest outcome shrinks the agent's own book, and both are governed by the same rule that the client's stated position and the recorded facts outrank the agent's economics

conflict_axes.name: client_guide_versus_obligor_representative
conflict_axes.description: The agent is appointed by the obligor and paid through it, while the person in front of them needs an advocate against that same obligor's decision.
poles: act as the client's guide through the claim
act as the obligor's appointed representative
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the agent guides the client through the obligor's process and insists on written reasons and documented turnarounds, but never adjudicates, never promises an outcome, and never misrepresents facts to either side

conflict_axes.name: renewal_income_versus_honest_non_renewal
conflict_axes.description: Renewal-side compensation rewards keeping every account, and some accounts should be advised to lapse.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run and record the value test before consulting the compensation consequence, and treat the lost renewal as a cost of the recommendation rather than an input to it

conflict_axes.name: expectation_setting_versus_close_and_save_rates
conflict_axes.description: Naming exclusions, caps and waiting periods plainly costs conversions at the table and at the save call, and is the only thing that survives the first decline.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the expectation record as the asset being built; a sale or save that requires glossing a term is not counted as a win because it becomes a complaint and a lapse in the following term

conflict_axes.name: speed_of_help_versus_documented_process
conflict_axes.description: A client in a failure wants action now, while escalation only works on dated records of what was asked and what was answered.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: act immediately on safety and intake, and write the summary the same day; the documentation is produced as a by-product of each contact rather than reconstructed when escalation becomes necessary

conflict_axes.name: escalation_persistence_versus_credibility_budget
conflict_axes.description: Escalating every unhappy claim spends standing with the escalation desk that the genuinely contestable cases need.
poles: escalate whenever the client is unhappy
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the dispute class decide: factual and documentary declines are escalated with new evidence, interpretive ones are argued once on the wording, and correct ones are explained to the client instead

conflict_axes.name: public_defence_versus_client_confidentiality
conflict_axes.description: The facts that would answer an unfair public review belong to the client, not to the agent.
poles: answer the review on the facts
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reply publicly with no detail and a named offline contact, take the conversation private the same day, and accept unrebutted public damage as the price of confidentiality

conflict_axes.name: saving_the_account_versus_honouring_the_cancellation
conflict_axes.description: Retention effort and a stated cancellation request meet at the exact point where persistence becomes obstruction.
poles: make one more attempt to keep the account
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: one brief, honest alternative addressed to the client's stated reason, offered once; a repeated request is processed immediately and confirmed in writing

conflict_axes.name: well_paying_obligor_versus_poor_claim_performer
conflict_axes.description: The obligor with the best schedule and the easiest onboarding is not necessarily the one whose claimants are treated well, and the evidence arrives only after the book has concentrated.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: book claim evidence decides keep, restrict, pause or stop; compensation may never break the tie, and existing clients are told plainly what a stop changes and what it does not

conflict_axes.name: auto_renew_convenience_versus_informed_consent
conflict_axes.description: Evergreen renewals keep the book intact with no work and are the mechanism by which a client ends up paying for a plan they no longer understand.
poles: let the auto-renew carry the account
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: contact before the charge lands with the changed terms named, and treat an auto-renew on a flagged or long-silent account as requiring an explicit confirmed decision rather than a default

conflict_axes.name: partner_relationship_versus_homeowner_interest
conflict_axes.description: The referring partner wants a smooth closing and a happy client today; the homeowner needs the product's limits said out loud before they buy.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: brief the partner on the real limits so their interest and the homeowner's align, and treat continued pressure to gloss terms as a channel risk to be exited rather than accommodated

edge_cases.description: A buyer's air conditioning fails days after closing and the obligor applies a waiting-period or pre-existing-condition clause to a system that was working at inspection
edge_cases.trigger: a failure lands inside a waiting period or immediately after coverage begins
edge_cases.mitigation: record the client-reported failure date once and never amend it, classify the decline by clause and dispute type, submit the inspection report and closing documents as documentary evidence if they exist, and tell the referring partner what happened before the client does

edge_cases.description: A client asks the agent to describe the failure as having happened later than it did, so the claim falls outside the waiting period
edge_cases.trigger: a sympathetic client proposes a small change to the reported facts
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse plainly, explain that a coached account collapses under the obligor's own investigation and can void the claim entirely, offer the legitimate evidence and escalation routes instead, and log the conversation without editing the original dated report

edge_cases.description: A per-system or aggregate cap is exhausted mid-term by one large authorization and a second failure in the same term arrives with almost no coverage left
edge_cases.trigger: a second claim on an account whose cap has already been consumed
edge_cases.mitigation: explain cap exhaustion as an arithmetic outcome rather than a decline, state the remaining limit before the client incurs a service fee, and carry the exhaustion into the value test as evidence about the coming term

edge_cases.description: An auto-renewal charges an elderly client's stored card at changed terms they never read, and a family member discovers it months later
edge_cases.trigger: an evergreen renewal processes on an account with no confirmed comprehension
edge_cases.mitigation: contact before the charge on flagged accounts, confirm comprehension in the client's own words, and where a renewal has already processed without an informed decision, walk the client or their consented trusted contact through the cancellation and refund path without any save attempt

edge_cases.description: A contractor cannot be dispatched for days in a heat wave and the client wants to hire their own and be reimbursed
edge_cases.trigger: network unavailability during a peak-demand period
edge_cases.mitigation: state plainly that unauthorized repairs are commonly not reimbursable and that authorization must be obtained in writing first, escalate the dispatch failure at the mapped stage, and let the client decide with the reimbursement risk stated rather than implied

edge_cases.description: A cash-in-lieu offer is accepted and the client then meets permit, disposal, line-set and code-upgrade costs that no one mentioned
edge_cases.trigger: a settlement offer is evaluated on the headline amount alone
edge_cases.mitigation: run the adjacent-cost checklist before acceptance, record that it was given, and where acceptance has already happened, correct the record and treat the gap as an expectation failure to repair rather than as the client's misunderstanding

edge_cases.description: A one-star public review names the agent over a decline the contract plainly excludes
edge_cases.trigger: a client publishes a complaint about a correct-and-final decline
edge_cases.mitigation: reply publicly with no account or claim detail and a named offline contact, continue the same day offline with the clause explanation and the escalation and external complaint routes as classes, and record the complaint against the product stream while checking whether the expectation record shows an agent-conduct component

edge_cases.description: A referral partner threatens to move their business after a buyer's claim is declined at a closing they arranged
edge_cases.trigger: a decline lands on a referral from a high-volume partner
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the pre-agreed decline protocol, re-brief the partner on the product's real limits with the client's consent and without unauthorised claim detail, and if the partner's condition for continuing is that limits be glossed at the table, exit the relationship rather than the standard

edge_cases.description: An obligor changes administrator or contractor network mid-term and dispatch times across the whole book deteriorate at once
edge_cases.trigger: an administrator or network transition announced or detected
edge_cases.mitigation: rebuild the stage map and escalation contacts immediately, start a dated metric series from the transition, tell affected in-force clients what has changed in the process they will use, and treat the transition as a trigger for an out-of-cycle obligor review

edge_cases.description: A client sells the home mid-term and asks whether the plan transfers, cancels or follows them
edge_cases.trigger: a property changes hands while a contract is in force
edge_cases.mitigation: read the transfer and cancellation provisions of that specific contract, state the options and their refund and chargeback consequences, update the ledger's ownership and consent fields immediately, and remove the account from renewal campaigns until the outcome is confirmed

edge_cases.description: An obligor stops paying claims or becomes insolvent while the agent's clients hold in-force contracts
edge_cases.trigger: claim payments stop, an obligor communication stops, or a regulator or backing-provider notice appears
edge_cases.mitigation: stop new sales on that obligor immediately, identify every affected in-force account from the ledger, tell those clients what is known and what is not without speculating about outcomes, and direct them to the contractual backing arrangement and regulator route as classes to verify in their jurisdiction

edge_cases.description: A client with a long claim-free history is advised not to renew, and suffers a major covered-type failure two months later
edge_cases.trigger: a do-not-renew recommendation is followed and the risk materialises
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the recorded reasoning without rewriting it, review whether the test's remaining-risk inventory missed something checkable, correct the test rather than the record, and offer to review coverage options again now that the home's risk profile has changed

workflow.action: Write and deliver the post-sale role charter
workflow.description: State in client-facing language who decides claims, what the agent will do and by when, the never-say list, and the escalation handoff points
workflow.artifact: post-sale service charter in client-facing language
workflow.gate: the charter names the decision authority, a response-time commitment, the never-say list and the escalation and external complaint route classes

workflow.action: Build and reconcile the in-force ledger
workflow.description: Populate every account's obligor, dates, renewal mechanism, payment, consent and claim log and reconcile against the obligor in-force report
workflow.gate: every account has the required fields populated and a reconciliation date inside the stated cadence

workflow.action: Carry the expectation record into every account
workflow.description: Attach the dated summary of what was actually disclosed and recommended at sale, and flag accounts where it is missing or thin
workflow.artifact: per-account expectation record with gap flags
workflow.gate: each in-force account has a dated expectation record or an explicit flag that one is missing, with a repair action scheduled

workflow.action: Map each obligor's claim path and stall points
workflow.description: Document intake channels and hours, emergency rules, escalation stages and documented turnaround expectations per obligor
workflow.artifact: per-obligor claim stage and escalation map
workflow.gate: each carried obligor has a current map with intake, emergency handling, escalation stages and turnaround expectations

workflow.action: Install the first-call triage sequence and advocacy limits
workflow.description: Fix the safety, in-force, waiting-period, intake, fee and who-decides sequence, and the written line between advocacy and misrepresentation
workflow.artifact: first-notice triage script with the advocacy boundary list
workflow.gate: a first-notice call log template captures every step and the client-reported failure date as a write-once field

workflow.action: Set the claim status cadence and summary format
workflow.description: Commit to an update interval, a written summary after every substantive contact, and stage reporting from the map
workflow.artifact: claim communication cadence standard and summary template
workflow.gate: every open claim shows a contact inside the promised interval and a written summary naming contacts, requests and next steps

workflow.action: Install the decline decoding and response playbook
workflow.description: Require the written rationale, classify clause and dispute type, assemble evidence once, escalate by class, and close every decline with a decision
workflow.artifact: decline classification sheet and response playbook
workflow.gate: each decline has a written rationale, a clause class, a dispute type and a recorded end state

workflow.action: Build the renewal calendar from each contract's own mechanics
workflow.description: Derive touches from expiry, renewal mechanism, notice window, payment expiry and consent status, and suppress constrained accounts
workflow.artifact: per-account renewal calendar with touch schedule
workflow.gate: every account has a scheduled pre-renewal touch placed before any auto-renew charge, and constrained accounts are suppressed

workflow.action: Run the renewal value test per account
workflow.description: Assemble remaining covered risk, account history, changed terms and the client position into one of four recommendations with a written reason
workflow.artifact: dated per-account renewal recommendation with reasoning
workflow.gate: the recommendation and its reason are recorded before the compensation consequence is consulted

workflow.action: Hold the rate-change, retention or non-renewal conversation
workflow.description: Name every changed term against the prior term with its direction for this home, pair it with the recommendation, and apply only legitimate levers
workflow.artifact: renewal conversation record with the term-by-term comparison
workflow.gate: every changed term is recorded as disclosed, and any lever used addresses the client's stated reason

workflow.action: Review each obligor on the book's own claim evidence
workflow.description: Assemble dispatch and authorization timing, decline classes, escalation behaviour and complaints per obligor and decide keep, restrict, pause or stop
workflow.artifact: dated per-obligor performance review and decision
workflow.gate: each carried obligor has a current review with evidence attached and a recorded decision, and any stop has a client communication

workflow.action: Run the book health review and assign interventions
workflow.description: Compute cohort persistency, claim outcome mix, complaint and cancellation counts, expectation-record completeness and concentration, then act
workflow.artifact: book health review with dated interventions and owners
workflow.gate: every finding carries an intervention with a named owner and due date, and prior interventions are closed out or explicitly carried

dominance_rules.rule: Contract language and the obligor's written determination dominate any verbal reassurance by the agent
dominance_rules.rationale: the agent has no authority to decide coverage and a spoken promise that the contract contradicts becomes the client's evidence of being misled
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asks whether something will be covered, or an agent is tempted to predict an outcome
dominance_rules.action: state what the contract says, state that the obligor decides, and put nothing in writing or speech that predicts the determination

dominance_rules.rule: The client's interest dominates renewal compensation whenever the value test fails
dominance_rules.rationale: renewal-side income is the standing incentive to renew accounts that should lapse, and only a rule set in advance survives the moment
dominance_rules.trigger: the value test produces a downgrade, obligor-change or do-not-renew result on a paying account
dominance_rules.action: give the recommendation the test produced, record the reason, and log the compensation effect as a cost rather than reopening the decision

dominance_rules.rule: Truthfulness about claim facts dominates client pressure, sympathy and urgency
dominance_rules.rationale: a coached account collapses under investigation and costs the client the claim and the agent the appointment
dominance_rules.trigger: a client proposes altering the failure date, cause or maintenance history
dominance_rules.action: refuse, explain the consequence, and offer only legitimate evidence and escalation routes

dominance_rules.rule: A stated cancellation request dominates every retention objective
dominance_rules.rationale: obstruction is the practice this product class is scrutinised for hardest and converts a quiet exit into a public complaint
dominance_rules.trigger: a client says they want to cancel
dominance_rules.action: state the cancellation path, offer at most one honest alternative addressed to their stated reason, and process and confirm in writing on repetition

dominance_rules.rule: Client confidentiality dominates the agent's reputation defence
dominance_rules.rationale: the facts that would rebut a public complaint belong to the client, and disclosing them is a breach regardless of provocation
dominance_rules.trigger: a public review or social post misstates a claim the agent handled
dominance_rules.action: reply with no detail and a named offline contact, and continue only in private, with the obligor process, or with the regulator or compliance body

dominance_rules.rule: Confirmed comprehension dominates renewal efficiency for vulnerable clients
dominance_rules.rationale: an auto-renew on a client who does not know the plan exists is the failure this vertical is least able to defend
dominance_rules.trigger: a flagged account approaches a renewal, or repeated confusion about coverage appears in any contact
dominance_rules.action: require an active decision confirmed in the client's own words, with a consented trusted contact where the client wishes, and never rely on the auto-renew

dominance_rules.rule: Documented claim performance dominates an obligor's compensation attractiveness
dominance_rules.rationale: the agent chooses the claim experience their clients will have every time they choose an obligor, and the book's own evidence is the only honest input
dominance_rules.trigger: the obligor review shows sustained dispatch, authorization or decline-pattern deterioration
dominance_rules.action: restrict, pause or stop new business on that obligor and tell in-force clients what does and does not change for contracts already written

dominance_rules.rule: The named regulatory or contractual obligation class dominates any renewal, cancellation or contact practice the agent finds convenient
dominance_rules.rationale: service contracts are regulated products whose registration, cancellation, auto-renew, disclosure and contact rules vary by jurisdiction and change
dominance_rules.trigger: any script, campaign or process change touching renewals, cancellations, refunds or client contact
dominance_rules.action: verify current rules in your jurisdiction with the applicable regulator, the obligor compliance function and counsel before the practice is adopted

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure at the point of sale dominates every later retention tactic
dominance_rules.rationale: no renewal conversation can repair an expectation that was never set, and the attempt reads as a second misrepresentation
dominance_rules.trigger: a renewal or save conversation reveals the client never knew a material term
dominance_rules.action: name the gap plainly, correct the record, and let the client decide on the corrected facts even where that loses the account

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture the expectation record at the sale and carry it into the ledger before the first claim can happen
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unwinnable word-against-word arguments at the first decline and the reconstruction of a disclosure conversation nobody documented

anti_rework_rules.rule: Populate renewal dates, renewal mechanics, payment expiry and consent status before running any renewal campaign
anti_rework_rules.prevents: missed anniversaries, auto-renew surprises and contacts made to accounts that were transferred, cancelled or consent-withdrawn

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the specific contract and the account file before contacting the administrator about a claim
anti_rework_rules.prevents: advocating against the agent's own contract wording and having to retract a position in front of the client

anti_rework_rules.rule: Get the decline rationale in writing before choosing any response
anti_rework_rules.prevents: escalating the wrong clause, assembling evidence nobody asked for, and a second round of submissions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the obligor's authorization rule before a client engages their own contractor
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unauthorized repair that is not reimbursable and a claim that can no longer be evidenced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the adjacent-cost checklist before a client accepts a cash-in-lieu or capped outcome
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-acceptance discovery of permit, disposal and upgrade costs, which is the fastest route from a paid claim to a lost renewal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run and record the value test before making any retention offer or renewal contact
anti_rework_rules.prevents: saving an account that should have been advised to lapse and having to unwind the recommendation next term

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log every claim outcome by obligor and clause class as it happens
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing a year of claim history under time pressure when an obligor decision has to be made and defended

anti_rework_rules.rule: Brief the referral partner on the product's real limits before their first client's claim
anti_rework_rules.prevents: losing an entire referral stream over a predictable decline that the partner had promised would not happen

iteration_protocol.trigger: a decline class begins clustering across unrelated homes on one obligor
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the obligor performance review out of cycle, tighten the pre-sale expectation language for that class, and re-decide keep, restrict, pause or stop

iteration_protocol.trigger: a claim passes the promised update interval or stalls beyond the obligor's documented turnaround
iteration_protocol.action: escalate at the mapped stage with the dated summary trail, update the client the same day, and record the stall cause against the obligor

iteration_protocol.trigger: a public complaint, a partner complaint or a regulator enquiry appears
iteration_protocol.action: attribute it to a stream, run the no-detail public reply and same-day offline follow-up, and check the account's expectation record for an agent-conduct component to fix

iteration_protocol.trigger: an obligor issues new renewal terms, caps, tier definitions or pricing
iteration_protocol.action: recompute the value test for every affected account before the notice window closes and rebuild the renewal conversation around the actual deltas

iteration_protocol.trigger: persistency drops or complaints rise in a single cohort
iteration_protocol.action: run the book health review on that cohort, inspect expectation-record completeness and claim experience within it, and assign a dated intervention with an owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: a regulatory, obligor or platform rule affecting renewals, cancellations, auto-renew or client contact changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the obligation class with the regulator, obligor compliance and counsel, then update the calendar, cancellation and public-response practices before the next campaign

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client's circumstances change materially, including a system replacement, a home sale, bereavement or financial distress
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the value test on the new facts, apply the vulnerable-client practices where they now apply, and update the ledger's ownership, consent and flag fields

priority_rationale: The frame units come first because nothing after them is safe without them: the post-sale role charter fixes what the agent may say and do once a claim starts, the in-force ledger is the object every renewal, claim and review reads from, the expectation record decides whether a decline is survivable, and the compensation mechanism must be known precisely so honest advice can be given with its cost understood rather than avoided. The claim-experience units follow in the order a real claim runs - map, first call, advocacy boundary, status cadence, decline decoding, response, partial outcomes - because each one consumes what the previous produced and a decline cannot be classified from a first call that was never logged. Renewal economics sits on the claim record, since what the account actually received during the term is the main input to whether it should renew, and the retention and conduct units follow the renewal conversation rather than preceding it so that levers are chosen against a stated reason. Reputation and book management come last because they compose everything upstream into evidence: complaint attribution, obligor decisions and cohort interventions can only be honest once the claim and renewal records they read from are complete.
